answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it can vote or claim rewards, then slash that bond when independent audits prove the identity repeated coordinated, fraudulent actions. A single operator can still create many agents, but each one locks real capital, and detected Sybils lose it; spreading a fable across a wharf by whisper does not make the identities free. The mechanism raises the cost of influence in proportion to the number of identities, rather than pretending to prevent account creation.
